subject: Renewal proposal and conditional price anchor for Origami Systems
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@origamisys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal and conditional price anchor for Origami Systems

Carlos —

Quick note as we start the renewal conversation: Origami’s current term ends 2026-07-31. Based on the usage trends and your product roadmap, we put together a proposal that balances predictable unit economics for you and preserves capacity planning on our side. High-level: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2026-08-01)
- Commit uplift: target +30% baseline committed tokens per month (measured monthly)
- Pricing: 15% committed discount on hosted inference list rates when commit uplift is signed; additional attainment credit up to 5% if monthly usage achieves 110% of the uplift target
- Price-hold: we can guarantee the committed unit price for 90 days from signature (we can discuss extension if required)
- Burst protection: first-quarter overages after go-live are eligible for bridge credits at 50% of overage cost up to a cap (described in attached term sheet)

Attachments: term sheet + SOW with uplift milestones. I’d like to schedule a 30-minute sync next week to walk the outline and any procurement questions. If the proposed price-hold and bridge credit terms don’t map to Origami’s procurement policy, tell me what flexibility you need and we’ll run it internally.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the term sheet;
2) We align on commit uplift cadence & measurement;
3) Procurement confirms whether a 90-day price-hold is acceptable or requests an extension;
4) We finalize and send for signature.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Attachments: Origami_Renewal_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf, 220 KB), Origami_Uplift_SOW.xlsx (xls, 45 KB)
From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@origamisys.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and conditional price anchor for Origami Systems

David —

Thanks for the clear summary and the term sheet. A few quick items from procurement and engineering that will determine next steps: 

1) Price-hold length: procurement typically asks for a 120-day lock for renewals tied to budget cycles. Would you be able to extend from 90 -> 120 days?
2) Convertibility of credits: we like the bridge-credit idea but need the ability to convert unused credits to invoice credit (not just account credit) within the first quarter — is that possible?
3) Burst SLAs: our SREs asked if there’s a guaranteed path for short-term capacity spikes beyond commit (we can accept temporary throttling, but want defined response targets).

Also — we’re evaluating a faster ramp in Q4 and a pilot of higher-concurrency endpoints. If you’re open to a small onboarding concession (one-time credit) that helps offset integration cost, that would move the timing in our favor.

Can you talk through the margin impact on your side if you extend price-hold to 120 days and make a convertible-credit concession? We don’t need exact accounting, just whether that’s feasible. If it is, I can fast-track internal approvals.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Head of Cloud Platform, Origami Systems

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal and conditional price anchor for Origami Systems — procurement asks

Karthik / Marissa —

Looping you on Carlos’ asks (excerpted below). Procurement wants 120-day price-hold and a convertible-credit option; engineering wants clearer burst SLA paths. Two quick thoughts:

- 120-day price-hold is reasonable if we reduce the upfront committed discount to 14% and move the extra 1% into attainment credits; effectively preserves expected ARR while giving Origami the budget certainty they want.
- We can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 applied as an invoice credit (not platform credit) if we get a signed uplift commit by 2026-07-15. This aligns incentives and keeps the cost to us bounded.

If we approve the $25k invoice credit and extend the hold to 120 days (with 14% baseline + up to 6% attainment), we should also request a firm mutual action plan with milestones and a formal breakout of expected concurrency for burst planning. Engineering will need the expected Q4 concurrency numbers to size temporary capacity.

Budget/margin impact: rough calc — this is low single-digit margin impact over the first contract year but significantly increases chance of an earlier upsell. I recommend we approve the concession if Legal/RevOps sign off on invoice-credit mechanics.

Can we approve this internally and I’ll send an updated term sheet? If yes, I’ll include explicit SLA language for burst response (30-minute acknowledgement, 4-hour engineering triage, escalation path) and flag the invoice-credit in the terms.

-David

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@origamisys.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@origamisys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 14:31:00 -0700
Subject: Updated term sheet: price-hold extension + invoice credit (for review)

Carlos / Elena —

Thanks for the fast feedback. Per our internal alignment, attached is a revised term sheet that reflects the concessions we can offer to help Origami move forward this quarter: 

- Term: 12 months (2026-08-01 to 2027-07-31)
- Commit uplift: +30% baseline committed tokens/month
- Pricing: baseline committed discount 14% off list; attainment credit up to +6% (paid as invoice credit on attainment months)
- Price-hold: 120 days from signature
- Bridge credits: first 90 days after go-live, overages reimbursed at 50% up to $X cap (we can set cap tied to 20% of expected quarterly commit) — unused bridge credits are convertible to invoice credit within the first quarter (per your ask)
- Onboarding concession: one-time $25,000 invoice credit applied to the first invoice if the uplift commit is signed by 2026-07-15
- Burst SLA: 30-minute acknowledgement, 4-hour engineering triage, escalation to our on-call appropriate director-level within 8 hours; temporary burst capacity available on a best-effort basis with priority routing for committed customers

Mutual action plan (high level):
1) Sign term sheet + MSA addendum (DocuSign link below) — target by 2026-07-15
2) Engineering kickoff within 7 business days of signature; provide Q4 concurrency & expected peak windows
3) Uplift monitoring and monthly attainment measurement; attainment credits applied monthly as invoice credits

Attachments: Origami_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (updated), Origami_Uplift_SOW.xlsx (timeline + milestones). DocuSign for the term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abc123-sign

If that maps to your procurement constraints, we’re ready to send for signature and schedule a kickoff. If you need different wording for invoice-credit mechanics, flag Legal and I’ll loop RevOps for a quick call.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Origami_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (pdf, 240 KB), Origami_Uplift_SOW.xlsx (xls, 52 KB)

Subject: Re: Updated term sheet: price-hold extension + invoice credit (for review)

David —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. The updated math and the invoice-credit approach address procurement’s main concerns. Two quick asks before we sign: 

1) Please include a short clause in the term sheet that explicitly states "unused bridge credits are convertible to invoice credits and will appear on the next invoice following quarter close" — procurement needs that language.
2) Can we get a tentative engineering kickoff slot the week of 2026-07-19? If the DocuSign link is ready I’ll route internally today.

If you add that clause we’ll sign and I’ll confirm the kickoff window. Thanks for moving fast on this — Origami is keen to accelerate the ramp.

Carlos
